walkthroughs.body_html:
Magnetism & Electromagnetism — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Magnetism & Electromagnetism brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Magnetism & Electromagnetism.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 2 kg object accelerates at 4 m/s². What is the resultant force?
options: 2 N
8 N
6 N

mcqs.q: What does it mean if the resultant force on an object is zero?
options: The object must be stationary.
The object is either stationary or moving at constant velocity.
The object is decelerating.
The object is accelerating.

mcqs.q: When energy is 'lost' as heat due to friction, what has really happened?
options: Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.
Energy has been used up and no longer exists.
Energy has been transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings — it's not destroyed, just dissipated.

mcqs.q: Why do transformers only work with alternating current?
options: Transformers work with DC too, just less efficiently.
A transformer needs a changing magnetic flux in the core; DC produces a steady flux and so no emf is induced in the secondary.
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
DC cannot enter a transformer because the iron core blocks it.

mcqs.q: Why does light bend when it enters a denser medium like glass?
options: Because the medium is denser, it physically blocks part of the light and forces it to turn.
Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.
Because it slows down — the change in speed at the boundary causes the wavefront to bend (towards the normal).
Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
